issue.title: Data providers in excluded classes unexpectedly run
issue.body:
| Q                          | A
| --------------------| ---------------
| PHPUnit version   | 11.4.1, 10.5.36
| PHP version          | 8.3.12
| Installation Method | Composer

#### Summary

Using PHPUnit 9, running `phpunit --exclude-group myGroup` completely skips testing classes with this group as expected. However, in PHPUnit 10 and 11, data providers in these classes still run, resulting in errors if the data provider depends on extensions or features not available on the current platform.

#### Current behavior

If a class is annotated with `@group myGroup`, and PHPUnit is executed with the `--exclude-group myGroup` command line option, data provider methods in excluded classes unexpectedly run, even though none of the tests in the excluded classes run.

If the data provider in an excluded class throws an exception (e.g. because it depends on an extension that isn't available), PHPUnit outputs the error, as well as the warning: No tests found in class "FooTest". This is very confusing since it was expected that the class would be skipped since it is in an excluded group.

#### How to reproduce

1. Add a data provider which throws an exception to a test class annotated with `@group myGroup`.
2. Add a test to the class that uses the data provider.
3. Run `phpunit --exclude-group myGroup`
4. Note the unexpected error in a class that is supposed to be excluded.

#### Expected behavior

Data provider methods should not run in classes that are in an excluded group.

This appears to be the same issue as #2922, which was fixed in 2017, but then the tests for it were inexplicably removed a few years later in #4570.
